# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Decompose the `downtime-worker.ts` god class

**File:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (8,105 lines, 174 exported symbols, 23 logical sections)

## Problem statement

`downtime-worker.ts` has grown into a single 8,105-line module that carries the
entire downtime-dispatch subsystem: constants, public types, idle detection,
the local-status poller, dispatchability gates, the Herdr list-head dispatch
pipeline, leader-election coordination, pane spawning and lifecycle, the worker
tick orchestrator, wl-output parsers, per-tier selection, settings clamps and
round-robin helpers. Navigating, reviewing and safely changing any one concern
requires holding the whole file in view, so every dispatch change carries
avoidable regression risk.

## Users

- **Downtime-dispatch maintainers (agents and humans)** need to change one
  concern (e.g. a gate, a tier parser, the spawn path) without reasoning about
  8,000 unrelated lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** need to review a focused diff where the blast radius of
  a change is legible from the touched module.
- **Future agents implementing dispatch work items** need small, named modules
  they can locate with a file search instead of reading a monolith.

Example user stories:

- As an agent implementing a dispatch-gate change, I want the gate logic in a
  dedicated module so that I can modify it without re-reading the whole worker.
- As a reviewer, I want a split diff to be attributable to a single concern so
  that I can verify it against its own tests.
- As a maintainer, I want each module under 1,000 lines so that the file is
  readable in a single pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports ≤1,000 for
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (now a thin barrel) and for every
   module created by the split.
2. **Public surface unchanged.** Every symbol currently exported from
   `./downtime-worker.js` remains exported from that exact path with identical
   types and values — the type-check passes and the 33 importing files compile
   with no import-path edits.
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change;
   no test file is modified (not its import paths, fixtures or assertions), and
   all 15 `downtime-worker.*` test suites plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite
   pass unchanged.
4. **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete
   sibling modules, never from the `downtime-worker.js` barrel; the dependency
   check reports no new cycles and does not extend the pre-existing
   `stalled-work ↔ downtime-worker` type-only cycle into runtime values.
5. **Single-flight state remains singular.** The module-level mutable
   `dispatchInFlightCount` (current line 2523) lives in exactly one module and
   is not duplicated by the split, so per-process dispatch single-flight
   semantics are unchanged.
6. **Responsibility documented per module.** Each new module carries a
   module-level doc comment stating its single responsibility, and the existing
   provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners) move with their code so
   traceability is preserved.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate code and update imports; do not refactor logic,
  rename public symbols, or change behaviour.
- **Barrel compatibility.** 33 files import from `./downtime-worker.js`,
  including 15 `downtime-worker.*` test suites (~15,000 test lines) and the
  production consumers `index.ts`, `settings.ts`, `ship-guard.ts`,
  `fetcher.ts`, `stalled-work.ts`, `worklist.ts`, plus 11 other test files.
  The barrel preserves that contract.
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf modules first (constants,
  types, clamps/parsers) and work inwards, so each merged step leaves the build
  and the full suite green.
- **No new runtime dependencies**, no test-file rewrites, no changes to the wl
  CLI contract or dispatch behaviour.
- **Scope boundary.** The item targets `downtime-worker.ts`; the other
  `packages/herdr` files above 1,000 lines are explicitly out of scope (see
  Risks — scope creep).

## Existing state

`downtime-worker.ts` is 8,105 lines. Its section inventory (line ranges from the
current `dev` checkout) is:

| # | Section | Lines | Size |
|---|---------|-------|------|
| 1 | Constants | 204–616 | 413 |
| 2 | Types | 617–709 | 93 |
| 3 | Idle detection | 710–862 | 153 |
| 4 | Idle-duration tracker | 863–902 | 40 |
| 5 | Per-slot idle tracker | 903–964 | 62 |
| 6 | Poller | 965–1248 | 284 |
| 7 | Dispatch (types + claim/result helpers) | 1249–2538 | 1,290 |
| 8 | Review-queue depth gate | 2539–2724 | 186 |
| 9 | Critical-only dispatch-window escape hatch | 2725–2776 | 52 |
| 10 | Herdr list-head filter dispatcher | 2777–3695 | 919 |
| 11 | Leader-election coordination dispatch | 3696–5614 | 1,919 |
| 12 | Pane-lifecycle monitor | 5615–5773 | 159 |
| 13 | Worker orchestrator | 5774–6932 | 1,159 |
| 14 | Blocked-questions prompt | 6933–6985 | 53 |
| 15 | Wiring helpers | 6986–7089 | 104 |
| 16 | Rotation-aware selection | 7090–7147 | 58 |
| 17 | Audit-tier selection | 7148–7307 | 160 |
| 18 | Implement-tier selection | 7308–7471 | 164 |
| 19 | Plan/intake selection | 7472–7510 | 39 |
| 20 | Critical-first selection | 7511–7804 | 294 |
| 21 | Dependency frontier resolution | 7805–7913 | 109 |
| 22 | Settings clamps | 7914–8034 | 121 |
| 23 | Round-robin helpers | 8035–8105 | 71 |

Relevant structural facts discovered during intake:

- **Module-level mutable state:** `let dispatchInFlightCount = 0` (line 2523)
  backs the per-process dispatch-pipeline single-flight gate.
- **Pre-existing coupling:** `stalled-work.ts` imports
  `parseDepListBlockersOutput`, `isAttemptBudgetExhausted`, `paneLabelItemId`
  and several types from `./downtime-worker.js`, while `downtime-worker.ts`
  imports `StalledPaneCandidate`, `StalledResumeOutcome` and `StalledScanOptions`
  types from `./stalled-work.js` — an existing type-only cycle that the split
  must not turn into a runtime cycle.
- **Precedent:** [WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO](../../../../.worklog) decomposed the
  2,584-line `src/database.ts` god class under ACs requiring an unchanged public
  API, tests passing without modification, and ≤500 lines per new module.

## Desired change

Reduce `downtime-worker.ts` to a thin re-export barrel and move its contents
into cohesive sibling modules, each well under 1,000 lines. A starting
decomposition (boundaries are an implementation decision, subject to the
constraints above):

| New module | Responsibility | Approx. size |
|---|---|---|
| `downtime-worker.constants.ts` | Tuning constants, floors/maxima, `decisionHeaderToken` | ~420 |
| `downtime-worker.types.ts` | Exported interfaces and unions (`LlamaStatus`, candidates, claim/result types, config, worker) | ~700 |
| `downtime-worker.idle.ts` | Idle detection, idle-duration tracker, per-slot tracker | ~255 |
| `downtime-worker.poller.ts` | `parseLlamaStatus`, `fetchLocalStatus`, `createDowntimePoller` | ~284 |
| `downtime-worker.gates.ts` | Soft-delete/assignee holds, review-queue depth gate, audit batch status, `classifyItemForDispatch`, attempt budget, critical-only escape hatch | ~480 |
| `downtime-worker.selection.ts` | wl-output parsers, per-tier selection, rotation, critical-first, dependency frontier | ~830 |
| `downtime-worker.clamps.ts` | `clampDowntime*` settings normalisers | ~130 |
| `downtime-worker.pane.ts` | Pane args/spawn options/spawn, pane-lifecycle monitor | ~360 |
| `downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` | Herdr list-head filter pipeline (`dispatchDowntimeWork`), prompt/comment builders | ~700–1,000 |
| `downtime-worker.coordination.ts` | `computeMostImportantItem`, `dispatchFromCoordination`, `runCoordinationCheckIn`, leader-election glue | ~1,000–1,300 (likely split into offers/leader) |
| `downtime-worker.orchestrator.ts` | `createDowntimeWorker` tick loop | ~930 |
| `downtime-worker.ts` | Thin barrel re-exporting the full public surface | ~150–250 |

Where a candidate module would still exceed 1,000 lines (coordination, dispatch),
it is split further along an existing section boundary rather than left oversized.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — reduce to a re-export barrel; preserve every current export.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts` — new; extracted constants and `decisionHeaderToken`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts` — new; extracted exported types/interfaces.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.idle.ts` — new; idle detection and trackers.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.poller.ts` — new; status parsing, fetch and poller.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — new; dispatchability gates and classification.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts` — new; wl parsers and per-tier selection.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.clamps.ts` — new; settings clamp helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.ts` — new; pane spawn and lifecycle monitor.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` — new; list-head dispatch pipeline and prompt builders.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts` — new; offer computation and coordinator dispatch (may split).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.ts` — new; `createDowntimeWorker` tick loop.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`, `settings.ts`, `ship-guard.ts`, `fetcher.ts`, `stalled-work.ts`, `worklist.ts` — verify unchanged (the barrel must keep them compiling as-is).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` — must remain unmodified; they are the behaviour-preservation gate.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — add a short module-layout note pointing at the new files.

## Related work

- **WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO** — *Decompose WorklogDatabase god class (src/database.ts, 2,584 lines)* (completed). Direct precedent: same refactor shape, same AC pattern (public API unchanged, tests pass unmodified, per-module line ceiling).
- **WL-0MUNMCZ2K003DZ50** — *F2: Wire drain signal to downtime worker dispatch* (completed). Recent functional change to the dispatch path; its tests are part of the regression gate.
- **WL-0MSZS1OHV0067JD1** — *Documentation: README update for `d` shortcut and `[Downtime Off]`* (completed). Documentation precedent for the dispatcher docs touched here.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — the dispatcher's behaviour reference; the module layout must stay consistent with it.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — herdr package overview; mentions the downtime worker.

Related work report generated by the `find-related` skill (full report:
`.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7.md`):

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO** – Decompose WorklogDatabase god class (src/database.ts, 2584 lines) (completed)
- **WL-0MUNMCZ2K003DZ50** – F2: Wire drain signal to downtime worker dispatch (completed)
- **WL-0MSZS1OHV0067JD1** – Documentation: README update for `d` shortcut and `[Downtime Off]` (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: break, class, downtime, file, lines (+4 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: break, class, downtime, file, lines (+4 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: break, downtime, file, lines, make (+3 more)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Barrel-induced runtime cycle (medium).** A module that imports from
  `downtime-worker.js` would create a cycle through the barrel. *Mitigation:*
  extracted modules import only from concrete siblings; the barrel imports
  downward only. Enforced by AC4 and the dependency check.
- **Duplicate or relocated mutable state (medium).** `dispatchInFlightCount`
  must not be copied into the dispatch and orchestrator modules, or
  single-flight would silently double. *Mitigation:* AC5 plus a targeted test
  assertion that the counter is shared.
- **Lost provenance / accidental logic drift (medium).** A large move invites
  silent edits. *Mitigation:* move-only rule, unchanged test suite (AC3), and a
  review pass that diffs moved blocks against the original.
- **`stalled-work` cycle widening (low).** The existing type-only cycle must
  not become a runtime import cycle. *Mitigation:* keep the stalled-work imports
  `import type` where they already are, and place
  `parseDepListBlockersOutput`/`isAttemptBudgetExhausted` in a module that does
  not import `stalled-work`.
- **Test-file temptation (low).** Updating 12 test files' import paths is the
  easy path but would erase the behaviour-preservation signal. *Mitigation:*
  AC2/AC3 make unchanged tests a hard gate.
- **Assumption A1 — scope.** The ≤1,000-line goal is the acceptance threshold
  for *this* item's outputs, not a mandate to also split `worklist.ts` (7,792),
  `index.ts` (2,784), `fetcher.ts` (1,579), `dispatcher-anchor.ts` (1,332) or
  `downtime-log.ts` (1,060). Those become separate follow-up items (see open
  question Q1).
- **Assumption A2 — compatibility.** `downtime-worker.ts` stays as a public
  barrel rather than updating its 33 importers (see Q2).
- **Assumption A3 — delivery shape.** The work lands as sequenced sub-items,
  one per extraction, each independently green (see Q3).
- **Scope-creep risk (explicit).** Splitting sibling files, adding a lint rule
  for file length, or reorganising the dispatcher's behaviour are all tempting
  and are **out of scope**; each is recorded as a linked follow-up rather than
  absorbed here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**OPEN QUESTION — Q1 (scope).** Is the "no file > 1000 lines" goal limited to
`downtime-worker.ts`, or should this item also split the other
`packages/herdr` files over 1,000 lines (`worklist.ts` 7,792, `index.ts` 2,784,
`fetcher.ts` 1,579, `dispatcher-anchor.ts` 1,332, `downtime-log.ts` 1,060)?

- Options: **(A)** limit to `downtime-worker.ts`, file follow-up items for the
  rest; **(B)** include all five in this item; **(C)** include `worklist.ts`
  only as a second phase.
- **Recommended:** A — the title and description name `downtime-worker.ts`;
  bundling five more files makes the item unbounded and delays the original goal.
- Status: unanswered (item auto-dispatched; no interactive producer).
- Assumption applied: **A**.

**OPEN QUESTION — Q2 (compatibility).** Should `downtime-worker.ts` remain a
public barrel re-exporting the current 174-symbol surface so the 33 importers
and 12 test suites need no changes, or should importers be pointed at the new
modules directly?

- Options: **(A)** keep the barrel (zero importer/test churn);
  **(B)** update every importer and delete the barrel; **(C)** keep the barrel
  now, plan its removal as a follow-up.
- **Recommended:** A — matches the WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO precedent and keeps the
  behaviour-preservation gate meaningful.
- Status: unanswered.
- Assumption applied: **A**.

**OPEN QUESTION — Q3 (delivery shape).** Should this land as one large change,
or as an epic decomposed into sequenced child items (one per extracted module),
each independently mergeable and green?

- Options: **(A)** epic with sequenced children, blocking order (leaf modules
  first); **(B)** a single big-bang change; **(C)** two changes (types/constants
  first, then the rest).
- **Recommended:** A — every extraction touches the same 33-importer surface;
  small sequenced steps keep the tree green and make review tractable.
- Status: unanswered.
- Assumption applied: **A**.

**Resolved by repository inspection (no producer answer required).**

- Q: How large is the file and what are its cohesive sections? — Answer:
  8,105 lines across 23 banner-delimited sections (inventory above). Source:
  `wc -l` and section-banner scan of `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`.
- Q: How many consumers depend on its public surface? — Answer: 33 files import
  from `./downtime-worker.js` (15 `downtime-worker.*` test suites, 11 other
  test files, and the production consumers `index.ts`, `settings.ts`,
  `ship-guard.ts`, `fetcher.ts`, `stalled-work.ts`, `worklist.ts` and
  `downtime-worker.fixtures.ts`). Source: `grep -rln "downtime-worker.js"`.
- Q: Is there an existing precedent for this refactor shape? — Answer: yes,
  WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO decomposed `src/database.ts` (2,584 lines) with unchanged
  public API and unmodified tests. Source: `wl show WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO --json`.
- Q: Is there module-level mutable state that a split could duplicate? — Answer:
  yes, `let dispatchInFlightCount = 0` (line 2523), the per-process single-flight
  counter. Source: line scan of the file.
- Q: Is there an existing import cycle to preserve carefully? — Answer: yes, a
  type-only cycle with `stalled-work.ts`. Source: import statements in both
  files.

# Coordination-mode batch continuation + deferred leadership hand-off

Parent AC4: on the production coordination path the leader must source continuation audit targets from its own Herdr head (bounded window extension, same ranking) without releasing leadership mid-batch, and defer the own-backlog leadership hand-off until the batch ends.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers parent AC2: Sequential single-audit safety: every continuation re-checks the idle-duration gate, `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`, proxy contention, code freeze, the active-audit markers and single-flight — no gate is relaxed, only the post-dispatch idle reset is deferred.
- Covers parent AC3: No duplicate or re-dispatched items: each continuation selects a distinct item through the existing classification and dispatched-marker exclusions, and any non-`dispatched` outcome ends the batch.
- Covers parent AC4: Coordination-mode compatibility: the leader sources continuation targets from its own Herdr head without releasing leadership mid-batch, and hands off leadership once at batch end.

- **Continuation source (AC4).** After a successful batch-eligible audit dispatch, `dispatchFromCoordination` may dispatch the next audit target from the leader's own head extension (`getHerdrListHead` + `fetchExtendedHerdrItems`, `includeNonCritical` filter as today) instead of only after total offer-list exhaustion — still exactly one dispatch per invocation, never two.
- **Same filters (AC3/AC4).** Every own-head continuation passes the identical sequential filters as the existing own-backlog fallback: `classifyItemForDispatch`, dispatched-marker exclusion (id-guard + staleness), attempt budget, non-terminal cooldown, code-freeze, audit slot minimum (≥2), in-flight critical guard, review-queue hold for implements. The continuation selects only `audit`-kind items.
- **No duplicate target (AC3).** The item just dispatched, and any item already dispatched in this batch, is never re-selected in the same batch — enforced by the existing marker exclusion plus an explicit batch-local exclusion set, covered by a test.
- **Leadership timing (AC4).** An own-backlog (`ownBacklogDispatch === true`) audit dispatch during an active batch with budget remaining does NOT trigger `releaseLeadership()` in that tick; the step-down happens exactly once at batch end (cap reached, depth dropped, failed continuation, or the next tick when the batch is no longer active). A normal in-view dispatch is unchanged.
- **No regression.** Non-batch coordination dispatch, leader election/lease TTL, coordination check-ins, pruning and the offer path are unchanged; `dispatchFromCoordination` direct-API callers without `freeSlots`/`auditBatchMax` keep today's behaviour (fail-open).

## Minimal Implementation

- Thread `auditBatchMax` and the batch-continuation intent through `dispatchFromCoordination`'s options (a boolean/marker set by `tick()` when the batch is active, plus the dispatched-target set for the current batch).
- Factor the existing own-backlog candidate loop into a reusable helper so the continuation path applies the exact same filters (no duplicated filter chain).
- Add `auditBatchContinuation?: boolean` (and any needed batch metadata) to `DowntimeDispatchOutcome`, documented, so `tick()` can decide the leadership step-down and the idle-reset deferral without re-deriving state.
- In `tick()`, gate the existing `outcome.ownBacklogDispatch === true` step-down on batch-inactive (deferring it to batch end).
- Cover with the coordination-dispatch and orchestrator specs from C1.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts
- packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts

## Dependencies

- Depends on the depth/reset item (C3) for the batch state and outcome surface.
- Depends on the observability item (C5) for the continuation token contract.

## Deliverables

- Leader own-head continuation with unchanged filter semantics and deferred step-down, with green coordination-dispatch/orchestrator tests.

# Documentation: batch setting, activation rule, sequential-safety invariants and decision tokens

Parent AC7: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` and the settings reference document the new setting, its activation rule, the sequential safety invariants and the new decision tokens. All related documentation (incl. code comments) is updated and consistent with shipped behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers parent AC7: Documentation: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` and the settings reference document the new setting, the activation rule, the sequential safety invariants and the new decision tokens.

- **Dispatcher doc.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documents:
   - the setting (`downtimeAuditBatchMax`, default 2, clamped 1–5, `1` = legacy/off) — in the settings table (~§1638) and the configuration prose;
   - the activation rule (audit-eligible depth ≥ `browseItemCount` from the Herdr head + `auditBatchMax > 1`);
   - the sequential single-audit safety invariants (AC2 gate list — nothing relaxed, only the post-dispatch idle reset deferred);
   - the new decision tokens (`audit-batch-continue` and held/blocked variants) in the reason-token lists (~§60/108) and observations section;
   - the deferred own-backlog leadership hand-off (WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24 interplay).
- **README.** `packages/herdr/README.md` adds an operator-facing bullet for `downtimeAuditBatchMax` in the settings list (~§521) and notes the batching behaviour (sequentially within one idle window, at most one active audit) in the audit-dispatch section.
- **Code comments.** Comments in `downtime-worker.ts` / `settings.ts` / `index.ts` describing the batch mode, its lifecycle and trade-offs (incl. the proxy-busy caveat: the audit pane's own occupancy still resets the tracker; the deferred reset is only the dispatcher's own post-dispatch reset) match the shipped behaviour in C3–C5.
- **Consistency.** Every documented token, setting name and activation rule matches the implementation; a doc-consistency scan (C7) finds no stale single-dispatch-only claims.

## Minimal Implementation

- Edit the three doc targets and the code comments touched by C3–C5; cross-check reason-token lists, the settings table and the host-wide serialisation section (§1044).
- Verify the AC7 checklist against the shipped behaviour via the verification item (C7).

## Key Files

- docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md
- packages/herdr/README.md
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts (comment blocks)

## Dependencies

- Depends on the implementation items C3, C4, C5 having landed.

## Deliverables

- Updated dispatcher doc, herdr README and code comments, consistent with the shipped behaviour.

# Verification: full suite + documentation consistency (parent AC8)

Final verification slice for WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS. Confirms the full suite passes with the new changes and that all docs are consistent with the shipped behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers parent AC6: Test coverage in the herdr package: shallow depth keeps the single-dispatch idle reset; depth at or above `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = N` yields N sequential audits in one idle window; idle gates, the active-audit marker, the cap, the depth drop and dispatched-marker exclusion are asserted.
- Covers parent AC8: Full suite: the full project test suite passes with the new changes, at minimum the full herdr package suite.

- **Full suite (AC8).** The full project test suite passes with the new changes — at minimum the full herdr package suite — run via the test skill; a red tree is never pushed (build → test → commit order).
- **Doc consistency (AC7).** A scan of `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` and the settings reference finds no stale references to single-dispatch-only behaviour and no contradiction with the shipped batch mode.
- **AC traceability.** Parent AC1–AC7 each trace to a green spec/behaviour; any gap is recorded in a comment on WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS.

# Intake Brief — Reduce per-invocation cost of the transient `wl` processes (WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B)

## Problem statement (headline)

Every `wl` command spawns a fresh Node.js process that takes **0.6–1.7 s and 80–180 MB** just to boot (a bare `node -e ''` is 0.35 s / 58 MB): the CLI eagerly imports 40+ modules (commander, all ~35 command builders, plugins, runtime, `better-sqlite3`) before any command logic, and herdr panes + pi agents fire these one-shot processes continuously (30 s refresh ticks, 60 s `sync --if-idle` per pane, per-agent polls). Four concurrent `wl` processes were observed at 25–65 % CPU each — bursty, seconds-long, gone moments later. The shipped read-cache (WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3) cut *read work* (83 %) but deliberately left process spawning unchanged ("each invocation still spawns a wl process"). There is also an unbounded hygiene leak: `~/.cache/wl/state/` holds **216,228 one-file-per-worklog-dir counters (~890 MB, 216k inodes)** that are never pruned.

## Users

- **Herdr TUI panes / pi agents** — the heaviest spawners; every 30–60 s tick pays full process boot even for cache hits.
  - *As a herdr pane, I want cache-hit refreshes to cost near bare-node boot, so refresh cycles stop stealing core-seconds from the host.*
- **Operators / agents running ad-hoc `wl` commands** — every `wl create/update/comment/sync/next` pays the same boot cost.
  - *As an operator, I want `wl` commands to feel instant, so interactive and agent-driven use stops producing CPU bursts.*
- **Host administrators** — transient process bursts and an unbounded 890 MB cache dir degrade a shared Raspberry Pi / herdr server.
  - *As an admin, I want spawn load and cache disk bounded, so the host stays responsive.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **(AC1)** **Import budget on the fast path:** the cache-hit read path and `--version` must not load command modules, the DB runtime, or plugins. Measured on the reference host (this repo, node ≥ 20): p95 wall time for a warm repeated `wl next --json` / `list --status open --json` cache hit ≤ **0.5 s** and peak RSS ≤ **60 MB** (current: ~0.6–1.2 s / 80–160 MB; bare node 0.35 s / 58 MB — the margin is deliberately tiny, so the fast-path import set must be slimmer than today's `read-cache-cli` graph at 61 MB). Enforced by a regression benchmark/test (e.g. asserts the heavy modules are not imported on the fast path).
- **(AC2)** **Measurable spawn-load reduction:** total CPU-seconds per 30 s refresh cycle across ≥ 4 panes on one shared worklog dir drops **≥ 60 %** versus current behaviour, measured by extending the env-gated spawn instrumentation (`WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE`, src/spawn-counter.ts) to record per-process CPU time (`process.resourceUsage().user+system`); baseline and after numbers quoted in the work item.
- **(AC3)** **Cache hygiene / bounded on-disk state:** `~/.cache/wl/state/` (216,228 files, ~890 MB, one file per worklog dir ever seen) is bounded and prunable — after a run, state storage is capped (bounded file count, or consolidated storage) and stale entries are removed; a documented maintenance path (`wl doctor cache` or automatic pruning) reclaims it. Freshness semantics unchanged (no correctness regression).
- **(AC4)** **No correctness regression:** all read-cache invariants from WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 hold — write→read freshness, arg-variant separation, WAL-aware invalidation, concurrent readers/writers, byte-identical JSON for identical (dir, argv, version). The existing read-cache/e2e/spawn-reduction suites pass unchanged.
- **(AC5)** **Graceful degradation:** if lazy loading or the split entry point fails for any command, behaviour falls back to today's fully-registered CLI (no functional regression, help/plugin registration intact).
- **(AC6)** **Tests + docs:** unit/integration/benchmark tests cover the fast path, lazy loading, CPU-time instrumentation and cache hygiene; related documentation (CLI.md / CONFIG.md / docs as appropriate) updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **Stateless one-shot CLI** — no daemon, no long-lived server, no IPC worker (operator decision, Q1-A). Architecture and on-disk Git/JSONL sync semantics must not change.
- `wl` must keep working from any worktree/`--worklog-dir` (the prefix-to-sibling resolution and worklog-dir override must not be disturbed by splitting the entry point).
- Cache correctness invariants (WAL aware, TTL 30 s, LRU bound) are **non-negotiable** — the fast path only shortens import time.
- Node ESM, build via `tsc` to `dist/`; `/usr/local/bin/wl` symlinks into this repo's `dist/cli.js` (v1.0.22) — keep that contract intact.
- Performance benchmarks must be CPU-time based / tolerant on shared hosts (a Raspberry Pi, herdr server).

## Existing state

- Read-cache epic **shipped (WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3, v1.0.9)**: identical JSON reads (list/next/show/search/status) served pre-parse from `~/.cache/wl` with 83 % read-work reduction, sync+heartbeat, herdr in-process memoisation. Its audit records the accepted variance: "each invocation still spawns a wl process that exits without DB work" — the spawn itself was left in scope.
- pi-extension poll gating shipped (WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N + tests WL-0MSB446N4009FFT5); orphaned worktree process lifecycle shipped (WL-0MRP1SLZB005ZNYO).
- Herdr cadence: 30 s refresh × 4–5 wl fetches per pane, 60 s auto-sync with 45 s cross-instance heartbeat (packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts).
- Measured here: `node -e ''` 0.35 s/58 MB; `wl --version` 0.95 s/80 MB; `wl list --json` (repeated) 0.6–1.2 s/80–160 MB; `wl status` 1.74 s/180 MB; `wl sync --if-idle` 1.39 s/116 MB; importing `dist/cli-utils.js` alone 0.60 s/73 MB; `dist/read-cache-cli.js` 0.46 s/61 MB.

## Desired change

1. **Split the entry point:** keep `src/cli.ts` thin — argv scan + read-cache fast path (imports only `read-cache-cli`, `spawn-counter`, `worklog-paths` + minimal utils), then **dynamically import** the current heavy graph (`./cli-main.ts` or lazy command map). Cache hits and `--version` exit before commander/DB/plugins load.
2. **Lazy per-command imports:** replace the 35 eager `import XCommand` lines with a registry resolving each command on demand; `--help` / bare invocation may load all (rare).
3. **Extend spawn instrumentation** with per-process CPU time (ru_utime/ru_stime) to measure CPU-second reduction, not just spawn count.
4. **Cache hygiene:** bound/prune `~/.cache/wl/state/` (e.g. LRU/TTL over counter files, consolidate counters, housekeeping in `wl doctor`); optionally tidy stale top-level entries.
5. **If ≥60 % CPU-second reduction is not reached by import slimming alone** (spawn count unchanged), coalesce repeated herdr reads into fewer wl invocations (still stateless, e.g. one batch query per refresh tick) — record which lever was needed.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/cli.ts` — split entry: 40 eager imports (lines ~6–47), cache fast path (~526–545) that currently runs only after the full graph loads.
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — cache lookup/backfill/invalidation orchestration; the fast-path import set.
- `src/read-cache.ts` — `state/` counter files (`stateCounterFilePath`/`bumpStateCounter`, ~157–200), purge/LRU, entry layout.
- `src/spawn-counter.ts` — extend `SpawnRecord` with CPU time.
- `src/commands/*.ts` — command modules to lazy-load (next, list, status, show, search, sync, …).
- `src/plugin-loader.ts`, `src/cli-utils.ts`, `src/lib/runtime.ts` — heavy imports to defer.
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — cache maintenance command (state pruning).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — coalescing repeated reads per refresh tick (only if needed to hit AC2).
- Tests: `tests/read-cache.test.ts`, `tests/read-cache-cli.test.ts`, `tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts`, `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts`, new `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts` / CPU-time benchmark.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSB19J56006E87J (completed, v1.0.7) — "Investigate excessive wl process spawning (206 concurrent, ~17 GB RAM)"** — the predecessor investigation. It attacked spawn *count* (pi browse-widget idle-gating → WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N, herdr cadence, read-cache). **Not a duplicate:** it left per-invocation *cost* and on-disk cache hygiene untouched; this item targets boot cost + `state/` growth.
- WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 (completed) — read-cache epic; the spawn cost was its accepted variance; this item continues from there.
- WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N / WL-0MSB446N4009FFT5 (completed) — visibility-gated polling in pi extension / herdr (spawn-count side).
- WL-0MRP1SLZB005ZNYO (completed) — orphaned node process lifecycle in worktrees.
- WL-0MRTSPLAX005Y8QY (completed) — process lifecycle documentation (reference for docs conventions).
- WL-0MULOZ37S007VV13 (completed) — metrics collection module (host metric collection precedent; candidate to reuse for CPU-second reporting).
- WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K (completed) — `wl sync` before refactor/standup skills (lock-aware `sync --if-idle` spawners).
- Duplicate check performed — no overlapping open/in-progress item targeting wl startup cost; `WL-0MSB19J56006E87J` covers the already-shipped spawn-count remediation only.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Lazy/help registration risk:** commander help and plugin registration must not regress — mitigated by AC5 fallback and deferring full registration to the heavy path.
- **Entry-point tests:** several suites import `src/cli.ts` / `dist/cli.js` directly; splitting must keep those contracts (tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts, inproc-harness, smoke, completion, …).
- **Benchmark flakiness** on shared hosts — AC1/AC2 measured by CPU time, p95 over repeated runs, generous margins above bare-node baseline.
- **State-dir pruning races:** pruning counters concurrently with writers must stay atomic (temp+rename, no regression of counter monotonicity).
- **Scope-creep guard:** daemon/server mode, JSONL/Git sync changes, and TUI redesign are explicitly out of scope — recorded as related opportunities, not work here.
- **Assumption:** the reference-host measurements above are representative of the failing hosts (same repo/worklog versions; herdr panes are the dominant spawner).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 — "What's the target shape of the improvement?" — Answer (rgardler): **A — keep `wl` a stateless one-shot CLI; lazy per-command imports, fast path for cache hits/`--version` at near-node-boot cost, plus cache hygiene (prune `state/`, bound growth). No daemon.** Source: interactive reply.
- Q2 — "How should we measure success?" — Answer (rgardler): **A — total CPU-seconds per refresh cycle ≥ 60 % reduction; per-process RSS < 60 MB; no correctness regression.** Source: interactive reply.
- Research summary: measured per-invocation cost (0.6–1.7 s / 80–180 MB vs 0.35 s / 58 MB bare node), attributed to eager 40-module import graph; verified the read-cache fast path still loads the full graph before serving (src/cli.ts); confirmed unbounded `~/.cache/wl/state/` (216,228 files / ~890 MB) with no pruning path.

## Related work (automated report)

Collected by `/skill:find-related` (sidecar: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B.md`).

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRTSPLAX005Y8QY** — Documentation for process lifecycle management (completed)
- **WL-0MULOZ37S007VV13** — Metrics collection module (completed)
- **WL-0MSB19J56006E87J** — Investigate excessive wl process spawning (206 concurrent, ~17 GB RAM) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — herdr cadence/spawner documentation
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — dispatcher/claim spawn context
- `CHANGELOG.md` — historical process-spawn/read-cache entries


---

## Plan — feature decomposition (plan skill, 2026-10-19)

Phasing is vertical slices (tracer bullets): measurement first, then the entry-point fast path, then cache hygiene, then the CPU-second verdict and docs. Each slice covers its own code, tests and docs; between phases, review the next items' descriptions and re-check the measured numbers.

| # | Child | Title | Type | Est. | Depends on | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | WL-0MVFRR98A008MM19 | Spawn instrumentation: per-process CPU and RSS | feature | S | — | Measure CPU-time and RSS per spawn (AC1 RSS, AC2) |
| F2 | WL-0MVFRRAXD001E7AN | Startup import-budget harness and baseline | feature | S | F1 | Ratchet + benchmark that lock in AC1 and capture the baseline |
| F3 | WL-0MVFRRCP7007UWS7 | Tests: thin entry-point split and dispatch parity | task | S | F2 | Test-first contracts for the entry split |
| F4 | WL-0MVFRRKKN00544PQ | Split CLI entry: thin fast path, dynamic heavy graph | feature | M | F3 | Fast path exits before commander/DB/plugins load (AC1) |
| F5 | WL-0MVFRREMZ0085G7I | Tests: lazy command registry, help and plugin fidelity | task | S | F4 | Test-first contracts incl. AC5 fallback |
| F6 | WL-0MVFRRMX3003UPP3 | Lazy per-command imports via command registry | feature | M | F5 | Load only the command that runs (AC1, AC5) |
| F7 | WL-0MVFRROLM002K98B | Fast-path import slimming to the 0.5 s / 60 MB budget | feature | M | F2, F4, F6 | Meet and freeze the AC1 numbers |
| F8 | WL-0MVFRRGGC001IQK1 | Tests: cache state pruning, bounds and atomicity | task | S | — | Test-first contracts for AC3 hygiene + AC4 freshness |
| F9 | WL-0MVFRRQ9W003KEFL | Bound and prune cache state via wl doctor cache | feature | M | F8 | Bounded `state/` store + documented maintenance path (AC3) |
| F10 | WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J | Verify >=60% CPU-second reduction per refresh cycle | feature | M | F1, F6, F7 | AC2 measurement and herdr-coalescing verdict |
| F11 | WL-0MVFRRTY5001KTNH | Docs: fast path, instrumentation and cache maintenance | docs | XS | F1, F7, F9 | AC6 documentation half |

### Plan-stage decisions (recorded assumptions)

- **D1 — Budget enforcement is a ratchet, not a single hard-coded threshold.** AC1's 0.5 s / 60 MB budget is tighter than today's fast-path graph (0.46 s / 61 MB), so F2 checks in a budget file (`bench/startup-import-budget.json`) that records the statically reachable graph and the measured cost, and fails on growth. F4 and F7 tighten it in the change that improves it — keeping the suite green between items while locking in every improvement and making the regression test deterministic and host-load tolerant.
- **D2 — Peak RSS comes from the instrumented child.** `process.resourceUsage().maxRSS` is recorded per process by F1, so AC1's RSS check needs no external sampler.
- **D3 — Cache hygiene uses a bounded LRU plus TTL over `state/*.json`.** Consolidating counters into the cache entry files is only adopted if the bounded-file approach misses AC3's cap, because the counter atomicity and monotonicity invariant (`bumpStateCounter`) is the freshness guarantee and must not be rebuilt.
- **D4 — Herdr coalescing is conditional, not assumed.** Desired change #5 is gated behind F10's measurement because herdr already dedupes concurrent identical reads (in-flight memo, WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG) and serves default-view reads in-process via `@worklog/shared` (WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B). The expected remaining gap is per-spawn boot cost.
- **D5 — `--version` uses the generated `src/version.ts`.** `getVersion()` currently lives in the 73 MB `cli-utils` graph; the fast path reads `WORKLOG_VERSION` directly so `wl --version` can exit at bare-node cost.
- **D6 — No daemon, no sync/JSONL changes** (intake Q1-A): the fast path changes only *when* modules load, never what is cached or how sync works.

### Appendix: planning-stage questions and decisions

Intake already recorded Q1 (stateless one-shot CLI, lazy imports, cache hygiene) and Q2 (CPU-second measurement, under 60 MB RSS, no correctness regression). The plan stage asked no new questions: the intake brief's measurements, desired-change list and answered decisions left no ambiguous choice that would change the decomposition. D1–D6 are recorded as assumptions for audit rather than as invented requirements.

- **OPEN QUESTION (for producer, non-blocking):** if F7 cannot reach 60 MB peak RSS (bare node is already 58 MB), should AC1's RSS limit become "within 3 MB of bare node", or should the fast path be allowed further Node startup work (e.g. a compile cache or snapshot)? F7 raises this with measured evidence rather than silently relaxing the AC.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-19 — plan skill: decomposed into 11 child items (F1–F11) in test-first dependency order; created all children at `stage=intake_complete`; wired 15 dependency edges; recorded decisions D1–D6; effort/risk re-estimated from the child WBS.

# F4 — Split the CLI entry: thin fast path, dynamically imported heavy graph

Implements desired change #1: `src/cli.ts` becomes a thin bootstrap (argv scan, read-cache fast path, `--version`) that dynamically imports the current heavy graph (`src/cli-main.ts`) only when a cache hit did not serve the invocation. This is the largest single lever for parent AC1.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/cli.ts` statically imports only the fast-path allowlist; `commander`, command modules, `plugin-loader`, `cli-utils`, `lib/runtime` and `better-sqlite3` load only through dynamic `import()` inside `cli-main.ts`.
- The F2 budget file is tightened in the same change: the recorded fast-path graph becomes the allowlist, so a future eager import fails the ratchet test.
- A served cache hit exits before any heavy module loads; `wl --version` prints the version from `src/version.ts` and exits without heavy imports.
- Every command behaves identically: full suite green, including `tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts` and `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` unchanged (parent AC4).
- Cache semantics untouched: cache key/argv extraction, TTL/LRU, WAL-aware invalidation, write-to-read freshness and byte-identical JSON (parent AC4).
- Worktree detection/process registration and the `--worklog-dir` override still run on whichever path executes; no regression for `wl` inside a worktree.
- The `/usr/local/bin/wl` → `dist/cli.js` contract is preserved; `npm run build` emits both `dist/cli.js` and `dist/cli-main.js`.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Move the current program construction, registration, help formatting, plugin loading and runtime initialisation into `src/cli-main.ts`, exporting an async `main(argv)`.
2. Keep argv normalisation, read-cache lookup, spawn recording and version printing in `src/cli.ts`; otherwise `await import('./cli-main.js')`.
3. Keep the write-invalidation hook on the shared path so writes still bump the state counter.

**Key Files:**
- `src/cli.ts`
- `src/cli-main.ts`
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts`
- `src/version.ts`
- `src/process-lifecycle.ts`
- `src/worklog-paths.ts`

## Dependencies

- F3 (tests first).

# F9 — Bound and prune the cache state directory via `wl doctor cache`

Implements desired change #4 and parent AC3: make the per-worklog-dir state counters a bounded, prunable on-disk store with a documented maintenance path, without touching freshness semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Opportunistic pruning on cache writes keeps `state/` at or under a configured bound (default file count around 1,000 plus a TTL for untouched counters, aligned with the existing entry TTL/LRU). Measured on the reference host: a pre-populated 200k-file `state/` is reduced to the bound by one prune run, with file count, inode count and bytes quoted before and after in a comment.
- `wl doctor cache` exists with `--json`, a dry-run (report-only) mode and a prune mode. It reports file count, total bytes, stale-by-TTL count and live-dir count, and reclaims space when pruning. Bare `wl doctor` mentions pending cache state.
- Pruning is atomic and concurrency-safe (temp+rename, never truncating a live counter mid-write) and never deletes a counter whose worklog dir still has fresh cache entries; if entries exist, they are invalidated before the counter is dropped.
- Freshness correctness intact: the read-cache suites pass unchanged (parent AC4) and no stale read is served because a counter was pruned.
- The cap is configurable (env var or config key) with defaults safe on a Raspberry Pi class host, and the default is documented.
- Covers parent AC3: `~/.cache/wl/state/` is bounded and prunable — state storage is capped or consolidated, stale entries are removed, and a documented maintenance path (`wl doctor cache` or automatic pruning) reclaims it, with freshness semantics unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add `pruneStateDir(cacheDir, { maxFiles, ttlMs, dryRun })` returning counts and bytes reclaimed.
2. Call it opportunistically and rate-limited (for example at most once per N minutes per process) from the cache write path, so growth is bounded without a daemon.
3. Add the `wl doctor cache` subcommand wiring the same function, reporting in text and `--json`.

**Key Files:**
- `src/read-cache.ts`
- `src/commands/doctor.ts`
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts`
- `CLI.md`
- `CONFIG.md`

## Dependencies

- F8 (tests first).

# F10 — Verify the >= 60 % CPU-second reduction per refresh cycle

Parent AC2's measurement and decision point. With F1 instrumentation, measure total CPU-seconds per 30 s refresh cycle across >= 4 panes on one shared worklog dir, before and after the fast path, and only then decide whether herdr read coalescing is additionally required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A repeatable measurement procedure is recorded (env `WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE`, 4 panes running the herdr query set over one 30 s cycle, warm cache) with the exact command quoted in a comment.
- Baseline and after numbers are both quoted in comments on this item and on the parent: total CPU-seconds, spawn count, cache-hit count, p95 per-spawn wall time and RSS.
- After <= 0.4x baseline total CPU-seconds (>= 60 % reduction) is demonstrated, or the shortfall is quantified with the dominant remaining cost identified.
- If the target is missed, the item records which lever is needed. ## Problem

`.pi/test-config.json` declares the canonical suite as `npm --silent test -- tests/cli` + `npm --silent test -- tests/unit`. Vitest therefore runs tests/cli (103 files) and tests/unit (43 files) only: the 76 root-level `tests/*.test.ts` files (`tests/read-cache.test.ts`, `tests/read-cache-cli.test.ts`, `tests/spawn-counter.test.ts`, `tests/audit.test.ts`, …) are never executed by /skill:test, implement.py finish, the pre-push hook, the ship release gate or an audit F3 auto-run.

## Goal

The canonical full suite executes every test file, or each exclusion is documented with a rationale.

## Acceptance criteria

- The canonical suite command(s) in `.pi/test-config.json` cover root-level `tests/*.test.ts` files, or each exclusion is documented with a reason.
- A full /skill:test run reports the root-level files as executed (currently 0 of 76).
- Root-level failures surfaced by the change are triaged into test-failure items.
- Documented in docs/dev/ (test-suite layout) so work items cannot claim coverage the gate does not provide.

Discovered from WL-0MVFRRGGC001IQK1 (F8 cache-prune tests), whose ACs reference tests/read-cache.test.ts / tests/read-cache-cli.test.ts passing — the canonical suite does not execute them.
